t.E538.agn: In 2018, EFSA saw no concern regarding genotoxicity or carcinogenicity; in a two-year study in rats it identified the kidney as the target organ and set a group ADI for sodium, potassium and calcium ferrocyanide of 0.03 mg/kg body weight per day, expressed as ferrocyanide ion. As the estimated intake remained far below this limit, it found no safety concern for the authorised uses.
t.E538.body: Ferrocyanides are poorly absorbed and do not accumulate in the body.
t.E538.found.0: Salt and salt substitutes (in the EU only in these, up to 20 mg/kg)
t.E538.prod: It is produced entirely chemically by the reaction of cyanide compounds with iron sulphate.
t.E538.regx.0: Re-evaluated; group ADI of 0.03 mg/kg body weight per day (as ferrocyanide ion); no safety concern for the authorised uses.
t.E538.regx.1: Only in salt and salt substitutes, up to 20 mg/kg.
t.E538.summary: Calcium ferrocyanide. It prevents caking of table salt.
t.E538.what: It is a ferrocyanide salt (calcium ferrocyanide) that prevents caking of salt.
